hero.title: Hi, I'm Èric.
hero.subtitle: Instead of showing you my GitHub and my code, here's a portfolio of my personal projects: the ones I build in my free time to explore, learn and solve my own day-to-day. A look at what I do when no one's asking me to.

about.title: Software, data and AI as leverage
company: I started as a software engineer building mobile front-ends, on Android and iOS. Then I moved to my current company, where I began with .NET back-end and some TypeScript front-end. Today, at the same company but on a new team, I work on AI solutions — and there I do a bit of everything: I think through the architecture, I code, I lend a hand with deployments and I act as a bridge between teams.

I find AI a hugely powerful technology, especially in solutions where it can amplify and reason in a safe, consistent way. It's not about putting AI everywhere: I start from the problem and think about how to solve it — and many of today's problems, the ones that need reasoning, lean heavily on it.
about.personal: In my personal work I touch a bit of everything. I've spent a lot of time on video automation, but also on automating my own day-to-day, on infrastructure and deployment, and on trying new tech non-stop. And underneath it all, always the same thing that drives me: AI solutions.
about.strength: If anything defines me, it's adaptability. On a foundation of software engineering and data science —and with AI as an ally— I move comfortably outside my own turf: I switch languages, keep making sense of code and project structures that aren't mine, and end up finding my way in unfamiliar environments pretty fast. That ability to adapt is my strongest point.

meta.title: ACG — Automatic Content Generator · Èric Casanovas Pérez
meta.description: A 9-microservice pipeline that generates and publishes short videos 100% automatically: LLMs, voice cloning, video rendering and publishing.

acg.name: ACG
acg.tagline: A pipeline that generates and publishes short videos (Reels/Shorts) — with automatic and semi-automatic flows.

voice.title: Listen to a voice generated by the system
voice.intro: One of ACG's cores is voice synthesis: I tried almost every relevant open-source TTS engine and built voice cloning on top of several. These are real samples from the pipeline.

problem.title: Producing social video at scale without touching a thing by hand
problem.body: A short-form channel constantly eats ideas, scripts, voice, images, editing and publishing. Doing it by hand doesn't scale. ACG turns that whole flow into a pipeline that researches, writes, narrates with a cloned voice, edits the video and publishes it — end to end, no intervention.

arch.title: From idea to published Reel
arch.caption: A central orchestrator coordinates the sources, AI generation, video editing and publishing. Each piece is an independent service.
arch.diagramAlt: ACG pipeline: an orchestrator coordinates data sources, AI generation, video editing and publishing.

flows.title: 8 flows, each a full pipeline
flows.intro: ACG's engine is plugin-style: each "flow" is a pipeline defined by steps, from the content source to publishing. Adding a new format means writing a flow, without touching the orchestrator. These are the ones built:

featured.label: See one flow from the inside
featured.note: From a hot Reddit thread to a Reel published on Instagram, TikTok and YouTube. Plays on its own.
captions: Jumps into Reddit and spots a thread that's blowing up
Pulls the comments apart: data, debate, agreements and pushback
Refines it all into a script with dialogue
Builds the video: background, character, subtitles and cloned voice
And it publishes itself — Instagram, TikTok and YouTube

showcase.heading: Pick a flow to see how it works

items.name: ACGAutomation
items.role: Orchestrator. Plugin-style flows + YAML DAG, dependency health-gating.

items.name: ACGAIAPI
items.role: Router of 4 LLM backends + 5 TTS engines with voice cloning + vision captioning.

items.name: ACGVideoEditorAPI
items.role: Video rendering: karaoke subtitles, thumbnails, multi-character conversations.

items.name: ACGClipForge
items.role: Semantic clip indexer to reuse footage.

items.name: ACGIGScheduler
items.role: Serverless publisher: uploads and schedules posts.

items.name: ACGManager
items.role: Human-in-the-loop panel: character builder and control.

items.title: Real microservices
items.note: A declarative dependency graph with health-gating: each service waits for its dependencies to be healthy before starting its flow.

items.title: Plugin-style flow engine
items.note: 7+ different video formats defined as YAML flows, without touching the orchestrator.

items.title: AI breadth
items.note: 4 LLM backends (cloud + local), 5 TTS engines with voice cloning, SD/ComfyUI for images, CLIP/BLIP-2 and semantic search.

items.title: Cost hacks
items.note: GitHub Actions as free cron and Cloudflare R2 as a no-bill S3. Self-hosted top to bottom.

honesty.title: Where it is today
honesty.body: ACG is a personal, self-hosted and working project, but right now on standby: I built it to learn how to orchestrate AI microservices end to end, and it did the job. The code is private; message me if you'd like a demo.

meta.title: Duna — My personal assistant · Èric Casanovas Pérez
meta.description: My self-hosted personal assistant: Google Calendar + Google Tasks + natural-language chat, in a single app, from 3 clients.

duna.name: Duna
duna.tagline: Calendar, tasks and natural-language chat in a single app I use every day.
duna.heroLine: I talk to it, it organizes my day: calendar and tasks, actually unified.

stages.label: You talk to it
stages.sub: voice or text, from your phone

stages.label: Duna organises and syncs
stages.sub: creates events and tasks for you

stages.label: You share and coordinate
stages.sub: a shared calendar with whoever you like

problem.title: Why I built my own assistant
problem.intro: Before Duna I tried a good handful of apps to get organized. None of them solved it all.
problem.hook: I needed something no app gave me in one place —and free, on top of that.
needs: Jot things down fast, by voice too
Add a location without the hassle
A shared calendar with my partner: see her availability and plan together

shot.caption: Add it by voice, in seconds
shot.alt: Duna in light mode, empty chat screen ready to type or talk

gallery.caption: List view, everything that's due
gallery.alt: Duna list view with upcoming events and tasks

gallery.caption: Month view, at a glance
gallery.alt: Duna month view with a selected day's detail

gallery.caption: And in dark mode, for the evening
gallery.alt: Duna in dark mode, chat screen

disconnected.caption: Before Duna: everything lived in its own app, and none of them talked to each other. Jotting something down meant opening two apps and doing it twice.

problem.solution: This is how Duna solves it

arch.title: Three ways to talk to it, one source of truth
arch.caption: I talk to it from the browser, my phone or Telegram. A central chat engine understands what I say and takes it to Google (calendar and tasks), storing locally what Google doesn't keep. All on my private network, nothing exposed to the internet.
arch.diagramAlt: Duna architecture: three clients talk to a central chat engine that syncs with Google and stores extras in SQLite, over Tailscale.

items.title: Truly private
items.note: It lives on my private network; nothing is exposed to the internet and the data is mine alone.

items.title: Like an app on your phone, with alerts
items.note: It installs on your phone and notifies you when it matters, even on iPhone.

items.title: Every morning, your day in one message
items.note: A summary of what's on that day, without opening anything.

items.title: Say a time, it creates an event
items.note: And if you don't say a time, it saves it as a task. A detail that changes daily use.

inside.label: Lovingly built under the hood
inside.note: TypeScript monorepo, dependency injection, network-free tests, hand-written CSS — all over Tailscale.

honesty.title: My everyday app
honesty.body: I use it every day so I don't have to rely on my memory: I jot down tasks the moment they occur to me, save future plans, doctor's appointments, the car's MOT… anything with a date I can't afford to forget. I talk to it by voice while I'm doing something else and it puts each thing in its place, calendar or task. It's not a demo: it's private, self-hosted over Tailscale, with nothing exposed to the internet. If you'd like to see it running, message me.

shot.caption: No tasks pending, all caught up
shot.alt: Duna's tasks view in light mode, nothing pending

meta.title: triagebox — Audio to ticket, solved by Claude · Èric Casanovas Pérez
meta.description: A microservice that turns an audio note into a ticket, and a Claude skill that reviews and acts on it. Generic, multi-tenant and reusable. Open-source and public.

inbox.name: triagebox
inbox.tagline: I turn an audio note into a ticket, and Claude reviews and fixes it for me.

story.title: From a bug on my phone to something fixed at home
story.caption: I hit a bug while using an app, dictate it on the spot, and forget about it. At home, Claude already has the ticket and works through it — without me opening an editor or typing a thing.

panels.title: I use my app and spot a bug
panels.sub: I'm testing it and something breaks.

panels.title: I dictate an audio
panels.sub: Nothing to open: I just explain the bug out loud.

panels.title: It's saved as a ticket
panels.sub: The audio goes to the cloud (triagebox) as a ticket.

panels.title: Claude fixes it at home
panels.sub: Next session it picks them up and acts one by one.

example.title: An audio instead of a forgotten note
example.body: I'm testing an app on my phone and spot a bug. Instead of losing it, I dictate it: "on the login screen, the Google button does nothing." By the time I get home, Claude Code already has the ticket, understands the problem, looks at the code and often leaves it fixed. The same works for a colleague reporting a bug with just an audio.

design.title: A pattern, not a closed product

items.title: Generic and multi-tenant
items.note: Several apps share the same triagebox via apps.yml; each with its own space.

items.title: Scoped tokens
items.note: Separate capture / read / write permissions: whoever records can't read or act.

items.title: Private network
items.note: Runs on the private network (Tailscale); nothing exposed to the internet.

items.title: Local transcription
items.note: faster-whisper locally: the audio never leaves home.

skill.title: Packaged to drop into any repo
skill.body: That logic lives as a Claude Code skill (/tickets) you can copy into any project: it reads tickets via API, classifies them and decides what to do — with an explicit security note against prompt injection, because the content comes from third-party audio.

honesty.title: My first public project
honesty.body: triagebox is my first open-source repo: public and designed for anyone to run on their own stack. The code is on GitHub, ready for you to drop the skill and the microservice into your own project.

story.title: I also code for the people I love
story.body: It's not all infrastructure and microservices. Some of the things I've most enjoyed making are for the people I love. This is an interactive website I made for my partner's birthday: it opens as a little experience, with scenes you move through one by one, sound and confetti. Handwritten HTML, CSS and JavaScript, no frameworks — just the wish to surprise her.

items.title: Interactive scenes
items.note: The site moves through scenes that the person discovers one by one, at their own pace.

items.title: Typography with character
items.note: Fraunces + Inter to give it a warm, careful feel, far from generic.

items.title: Sound and confetti
items.note: Small animation and audio touches that make the moment feel special.

items.title: Pure HTML
items.note: Handmade, no frameworks: light, fast and easy to host anywhere.

honesty.title: Code made with care
honesty.body: It's a small, personal project, but one of the ones I'm most excited to show: it shows I like to care about design and detail, and that coding also lets me make the people I love happy.
